Subject: Re: MAP: deployment mode & region evaluation for Medicore — technical tradeoffs

Hi Elena — quick technical note to help with the procurement delta ask. Below are concise, realistic tradeoffs and a recommended staged approach.

Summary of hosting options (short):
- Hosted (Redwood EU cluster): fastest to spin up for functional evals. Shared tenancy but can run in FR region; obfuscate PII for testing. Approx latency: P95 ~70–120ms depending on sequence length. Cost: low variable (pay-as-you-go).
- Dedicated (EU, Frankfurt): single-tenant GPU pools, VPC peering, encrypted at rest with customer KMS. P95 latency: ~40–90ms depending on instance sizing; predictable throughput and isolation. Operational onboarding: ~2–3 weeks plus network setup.
- Private (on-prem / customer VPC with private control plane): required only if regulators insist on physically isolated infrastructure; highest setup cost and longest lead time (6–10 weeks).

Recommended path for MAP (technical runbook items):
1) Short functional eval on Hosted (EU-FR) using synthetic payloads — validate prompts, stream handling, and basic latency.
2) Pilot on Dedicated (EU-FR) with VPC peering + customer KMS. Run acceptance tests below.
3) If regulator requires, prepare Private deployment SOW in parallel and collect security evidence.

Acceptance criteria (examples to include in MAP):
- Latency: P95 < 120ms for standard request profile (<= 512 tokens).
- Throughput: sustained 20 RPS with autoscaling headroom for burst to 100 RPS.
- Cost: pilot monthly spend not to exceed EUR 15k (to be refined).
- Security: SOC2 evidence, pen-test within last 12 months, network connectivity validated.

I attached a machine-readable hosting_profiles.csv with the rough perf/cost rows for the configurations we typically provision. Happy to jump on a short call to walk through the numbers.

-Karthik
